title: Understanding Your Time Blindness
instructions: Answer these questions to identify how time blindness affects your startup work.

options: Being too busy to track time
The ADHD tendency to poorly perceive, estimate, and track time
questions.explanation_markdown: **Time blindness is the ADHD tendency to poorly perceive, estimate, and track time.** It's a neurological difference in how ADHD brains process temporal information, not a behavioral choice or time management failure.

options: Work 3 times harder to meet deadlines
Multiply your time estimates by 3 to get realistic durations
Do each task 3 times to improve quality
questions.explanation_markdown: The **3X Rule means multiplying your time estimates by 3** to account for ADHD optimism bias and time blindness. If you think something will take 1 hour, plan for 3 hours. This compensates for systematic underestimation.
questions.hint: It's about adjusting your estimates, not your work intensity.

questions.prompt_markdown: **For ADHD brains, time often exists in only two states:**
questions.explanation_markdown: ADHD brains experience **NOW and NOT NOW**—a deadline next week and a deadline next month both feel like NOT NOW until suddenly they're NOW (urgent). This time horizon blindness makes it hard to start tasks until they become emergencies.
questions.hint: Think about how deadlines feel: either urgent or not urgent, with little in between.

questions.prompt_markdown: **Visual timers and Pomodoro technique help with which type of time blindness?**
options: Time perception blindness (losing track of time passing)
Time horizon blindness (NOW vs NOT NOW)
They don't help with time blindness
questions.explanation_markdown: Visual timers help with **time perception blindness**—they make invisible time visible, helping you see how much time has actually passed. This is especially helpful during hyperfocus when time completely disappears.
questions.hint: These tools show you time passing in the moment.

questions.prompt_markdown: **True or False: With enough practice, you can overcome time blindness and develop accurate time perception.**
questions.explanation_markdown: **False!** Time blindness is a neurological difference in how ADHD brains process temporal information. You can't 'fix' it through practice, but you can completely compensate for it with external systems (timers, tracking, 3X rule, etc.).
questions.hint: Think about whether this is a skill or a brain wiring difference.
